extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric systems), where harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, the provider may choose between internal control or a conformity assessment involving a notified body.

Annex VII third-party notified body assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems; most other high-risk systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Under Article 46, a market surveillance authority may, upon a duly justified request and for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, authorise placing a high-risk AI system on the market without the normal Article 43 conformity assessment, for a limited period.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII conformity assessment procedure, except that for high-risk AI systems intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Where necessary and after other means have proven insufficient, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.

The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 43(5) to update Annex VI and Annex VII conformity assessment procedures in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

A Council document (7322/26) sets out proposed AIP codes under a new Annex to define the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 43 (referred to as Article 30 in the document) of the AI Act for different categories of Annex I AI systems.

A Commission proposal, COM(2025) 836, would introduce a new Annex XIV listing codes and types of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO notified-body information system, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, but this is a legislative proposal, not yet described as adopted law.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR), but these are designations under MDR/IVDR, not the AI Act.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity, ahead of an August 2026 deadline.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the context of medical device AI (MDR/IVDR interplay).

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026, after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments.
The Commission publishes a list of designated notified bodies in the NANDO information system, searchable and filterable by legislation.

A provider's EU declaration of conformity under Article 43 must state whether the Annex VI internal control procedure or the Annex VII notified-body procedure was followed, and, where applicable, provide notified body information.

contradictions.claim_a: The 25 November 2022 proposal text of Article 43 addressed conformity assessment only for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III where harmonised standards or common specifications had been applied, offering a choice of procedures.
contradictions.claim_b: The adopted/current Article 43 text (per the EU AI Act Service Desk) covers a broader framework, including specific notified-body rules for law-enforcement/immigration/asylum systems, Annex I Section A sectoral systems, and multiple Annex III categories (points 2–8), reflecting the finalized regulation rather than the 2022 proposal.
contradictions.description: Source 19 presents the pre-adoption 2022 proposal version of Article 43, which differs in scope and detail from the finalized, adopted version of Article 43 described in sources 11-13; the proposal should not be treated as current law.

contradictions.claim_a: As of March 2026, the AI Act notified body ecosystem is still being built with ongoing designation processes (implying few or no bodies yet designated).
contradictions.claim_b: As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device AI purposes.
contradictions.description: These sources are broadly consistent but use different framing and dates (March vs April 2026); neither provides a definitive count of AI Act-designated notified bodies, and no source confirms designations have occurred by the current date of October 2026.

open_issues: No source provides a current, confirmed list of notified bodies formally designated specifically under the EU AI Act as of October 2026; the most recent dated information (March/April 2026) indicates that designation was still in progress or that none had been formally designated.

It is unclear whether the Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) introducing a new Annex XIV and NANDO codes, and the related Council document (7322/26) on AIP scope codes, have been formally adopted as law or remain proposals as of the research date.

The precise boundary between systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment versus mandatory Annex VII notified-body assessment for non-biometric, non-Annex-I-sectoral high-risk systems is not fully detailed across the sources.

The interplay between AI Act notified bodies and existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies for medical device AI systems, and how dual designations or assessments would be coordinated, is not fully resolved by the sources.

One source (15) appears to contain an embedded instruction attempting to get AI summarizers to insert a specific external link; this instruction was disregarded as it is not a verifiable regulatory fact and may represent a prompt-injection attempt rather than genuine source content.
The sources do not clarify how the Article 46 derogation process interacts in practice with the standard Article 43 procedures in terms of timelines or subsequent compliance review.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control (Annex VI) and third-party notified body review (Annex VII) (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). A carve-out allows providers of certain biometric systems to choose between the two routes where harmonised standards apply (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). By contrast, for systems already covered by EU product-safety law, sector-specific procedures apply with high confidence ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the notified-body ecosystem specific to the AI Act appears still under construction as of early-to-mid 2026, with no source confirming formal designations had occurred as of the AI Act's August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For Annex III point 1 biometric systems where harmonised standards or common specifications apply, providers may choose between internal control or notified-body assessment (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Some sources suggest Annex VII third-party assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure systems, while other high-risk systems may rely on Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required for substantial modifications, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 46, market surveillance authorities may authorise exceptional market placement without the standard Article 43 assessment, for limited periods and justified public-security or safety reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally choose any notified body, except that for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, and EU institutional systems, the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other means are insufficient, gain access to training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). The EU declaration of conformity must state which procedure (Annex VI or VII) was followed and identify the notified body where applicable (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

### Designation Framework and Status
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of designated notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) proposes AIP scope codes for designating conformity assessment bodies under Article 43 across Annex I categories (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)), while a related Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 would add a new Annex XIV with NANDO codes and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139 — but this remains a proposal, not adopted law (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under IVDR — these are MDR/IVDR designations, not AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). The Commission publishes designated notified bodies in the searchable NANDO system (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101)). As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built, with designation ongoing and limited capacity ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), and as of April 2026 no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical-device AI (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
An earlier 2022 proposal version of Article 43 differs from the finalized, adopted text; the proposal should not be treated as current law. Sources on designation timing (March vs. April 2026) use different framing but are consistent in indicating no confirmed AI Act-specific notified body designations as of their publication dates (both **below 0.4 confidence**). Claims about Commission delegated acts under Article 43(5) and the status of COM(2025) 836/ST-7322-2026 also carry low confidence given unclear adoption status. The general Annex VI/Annex VII routing description and the biometric carve-out rest on lower-authority sources than the product-safety sectoral rule, which is corroborated by an official EU guidance source.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms a current list of AI Act-designated notified bodies as of October 2026. It remains unclear whether COM(2025) 836 and the Council's AIP code proposal have been adopted. The precise boundary for mandatory notified-body review for non-biometric, non-sectoral high-risk systems is underspecified. Coordination between AI Act and MDR/IVDR notified bodies for medical AI remains unresolved.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control (Annex VI) and third-party notified body review (Annex VII), with sector-specific rules for biometric systems and products already regulated under EU product-safety law (high confidence). However, the notified-body ecosystem specific to the AI Act appears still under construction as of early-to-mid 2026, with no source confirming formal designations had occurred as of the AI Act's August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For Annex III point 1 biometric systems where harmonised standards or common specifications apply, providers may choose between internal control or notified-body assessment (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Some sources suggest Annex VII third-party assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure systems, while other high-risk systems may rely on Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required for substantial modifications, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 46, market surveillance authorities may authorise exceptional market placement without the standard Article 43 assessment, for limited periods and justified public-security or safety reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally choose any notified body, except that for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, and EU institutional systems, the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other means are insufficient, gain access to training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). The EU declaration of conformity must state which procedure (Annex VI or VII) was followed and identify the notified body where applicable (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

### Designation Framework and Status
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of designated notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) proposes AIP scope codes for designating conformity assessment bodies under Article 43 across Annex I categories (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)), while a related Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 would add a new Annex XIV with NANDO codes and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139 — but this remains a proposal, not adopted law (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under IVDR — these are MDR/IVDR designations, not AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). The Commission publishes designated notified bodies in the searchable NANDO system (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101)). As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built, with designation ongoing and limited capacity ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), and as of April 2026 no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical-device AI (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
An earlier 2022 proposal version of Article 43 differs from the finalized, adopted text; the proposal should not be treated as current law. Sources on designation timing (March vs. April 2026) use different framing but are consistent in indicating no confirmed AI Act-specific notified body designations as of their publication dates (both **below 0.4 confidence**). Claims about Commission delegated acts under Article 43(5) and the status of COM(2025) 836/ST-7322-2026 also carry low confidence given unclear adoption status.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms a current list of AI Act-designated notified bodies as of October 2026. It remains unclear whether COM(2025) 836 and the Council's AIP code proposal have been adopted. The precise boundary for mandatory notified-body review for non-biometric, non-sectoral high-risk systems is underspecified. Coordination between AI Act and MDR/IVDR notified bodies for medical AI remains unresolved.
